notes: The first batch from this source: sixteen environmental review documents published by the SF Planning Department between 1981 and 2008, picked to be the address-titled projects that are NOT downtown highrises, because downtown is what the collection over-represents and what the site is already best covered on. An EIR describes a site before a project, so it is a record of buildings that no longer stand, and it states the assessor's block and lot outright — the parcel comes free where every other source in the register has to be joined to EAS. What it says about the project itself is a proposal and not an outcome, so nothing here records what was built.

coverage.remaining: 156 of the 172 address-titled documents in the collection, and the ~617 that are titled by project or area rather than address. The unread address-titled ones are overwhelmingly downtown and South of Market office towers, 1975-2011.
coverage.note: 16 documents read whole. Fifteen yielded facts; 1055 Stockton yielded none — its EIR says neither building on the site was on any list of historical, architectural or cultural interest and gives no construction date. Every document but 2222 23rd Street states the assessor's block, and eleven state the lot as well.
